tone_statements.citation: Barreteau, Daniel. 1987 [offprint and IRD record dated 1985]. Du mbara au mofu-gudur: approche comparée des systèmes verbaux. In Jean-Pierre Caprile & Herrmann Jungraithmayr (eds.), Langues tchadiques et langues non tchadiques en contact en Afrique centrale: actes de la table ronde franco-allemande, Ivry, 8-12 décembre 1978 (LACITO-documents, Afrique 10; Contacts de langues et contacts de cultures 5), 37-60. Paris: SELAF. IRD Horizon fdi:010022407.
tone_statements.quote: Il y a une dichotomie très nette dans le système aspectuel du mbara où les trois formes d'inaccompli sont marquées par un ton haut sur les modalités personnelles et les deux formes d'accompli par un ton bas ; une telle répartition se retrouve en mulwi et en mafa : ton haut sur la marque personnelle à l'inaccompli, ton bas à l'accompli. [...] Comparativement, le mbara est d'un type beaucoup plus commun en ce sens que le schème tonal lexical est entièrement contenu dans le radical proprement dit.
tone_statements.translation: There is a very clear dichotomy in the aspect system of Mbara, where the three imperfective (inaccompli) forms are marked by a high tone on the person markers and the two perfective (accompli) forms by a low tone; the same distribution is found in Mulwi and Mafa: high tone on the person marker in the imperfective, low tone in the perfective. [...] By comparison, Mbara is of a much more common type in that the lexical tone pattern is entirely contained within the radical itself.
tone_statements.locator: p.45, sec. 3.9 'Les aspects'; then p.43, sec. 3.5; see also sec. 3.5 end (p.43: no voiceless/H - voiced/L consonant-tone correlation in Mbara), sec. 3.7 p.44 and sec. 3.12 p.47
tone_statements.summary: In Barreteau's presentation of Tourneux's Mbara data there are two tone levels (high/low, acute/grave in the transcriptions); verbs have a lexical tone pattern confined to the radical (no floating pre- or postposed tones as in Mofu-Gudur), the preverbal person markers have no tone of their own but carry H in the three inaccompli forms and L in the two accompli forms, so the aspect opposition is m…

sources.note: Five-page presentation of the Mbara verb system given at the Ivry 1978 round table, whose programme (Chadic Newsletter 9, read) was dominated by papers on tonal alternation/tonal inflection in verb systems (Ruelland, Caprile, Cloarec, Ebobisse, Monino); the title itself is tone-marked (mbárá). Likely gives tone-marked verb forms and states whether verb classes or aspect are distinguished tonally; basis is the record and the round-table context only, text not seen.
